To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lymphocytes, which have been transformed into blast cells by mitogens, can be transformed into a second type of blast cells endowed with cytolytic activity by the addition of a third substance, the mitogen itself, and that these cells adhere to fibroblast target cells.

lymphocytes which were transformed in culture to secondary lymphocytes by mitogen stimulation adhered specifically to fibroblasts in the presence of mitogen, and that these adhering lymphocytes were endowed with target-cell killing ability.
in vitro differentiated lymphocytes adhered specifically to fibroblasts and transformed to blast cells endowed target-cell lytic activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the adherence of lymphocytes to target cells and its possible role in cellular immunity.
the study of lymphocyte transformation in vitro and with its relationship to cellular immunity.
the specific adherence of in vitro differentiated lymphocytes to target cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adherence of lymphocytes to target cells in vitro is specific for the PWM-induced cells, and that this adherence is a prelude to target cell lysis.
the lymphocyte population is heterogeneous with respect to adherence and target-cell lytic activity.
the lymphocytes which were transformed by PHA, Con A, or PWM to secondary lymphocytes, and which adhered in the presence of mitogens to fibroblast cells, were endowed with target-cell-lytic ability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lymphocytes can be differentiated in vitro by the use of mitogens into blast cells and secondary lymphocytes which differ in their ability to adhere to monolayers and to kill target cells.
lymphocyte adherence to target cells is a specific process, which is a prerequisite for the development of target-cell lytic capacity.
the lymphocyte transformation and blast cell formation are not necessarily linked.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown for the first time that the secondary lymphocytes adhere to fibroblasts in the presence of the mitogen.

the lymphocytes which are derived from lymph node cells by transformation in culture, and which can be induced by mitogens to adhere to fibroblast target cells, are a suitable system to investigate cellular immunity in vitro.
the adherence of lymphocytes to fibroblast target cells in the absence of PWM is not specific.
